_note: v5.11: v5.8 + Troika-style primitive branches (Huang et al., CVPR 2024, 'Troika: Multi-Path Cross-Modal Traction'). In v5.8 one CLS embedding is matched against the pair, crop and disease prompts, so the crop and disease losses pull the same vector two ways. Here crop and disease each get their own visual features (model.primitive_branches), trained by the crop / disease losses, and at prediction time their scores are fused into each pair's score with weights chosen on validation (evaluation.posthoc). Two linked parts (branches + fusion, since the branches only change predictions through fusion); the run's plain-scoring and fusion numbers separate them, and v9 measured fusion without branches (+1.6 on one split, CI including 0). Troika's cross-modal traction module is not included. Compare with v5.8 (v5.5 recipe, same 3 validation splits, seeds 42-44): mean validation HM 59.75% (per split 56.48 / 62.10 / 60.66); keep only if the mean beats it by more than 2 points (> 61.75), ideally on every split. Never decide on test.
_result: KEEP by the rule, but mostly through fusion. Mean validation HM 62.23% over 3 splits vs v5.8 59.75% (+2.48), higher on every split: 59.73 / 63.88 / 63.08. Epoch 5, gamma 0.0325, fusion crop weight 2.0, disease weight 0.5. Without fusion (plain pair scoring) the branches give 60.73% (+0.98, within noise); fusion adds +1.45 points over plain on the same run (paired bootstrap 95% CI [+0.57, +2.30]). Compare v9 (post-hoc fusion without branches, +1.64). Test (reported, not used to decide): HM 68.23% (seen 56.50%, unseen 86.12%).
title: primitive_branches

model._note: Same OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16 (QuickGELU) as v4.1/v4.2; the text encoder stays frozen.

primitive_branches._note: NEW (v5.11): crop and disease visual branches, residual linear maps on the CLS embedding initialised to zero (dpd/primitive_branches.py). lr as the LoRA adapters.

image_encoder._note: From v5.3: v5 + more LoRA capacity: last 8 blocks instead of 4, rank 16 instead of 8. alpha 16 -> 32 keeps the LoRA scale (alpha/rank) at 2, so only capacity changes, not the effective step size. About 4x more adapter parameters (1.57M vs 393k). Same lr.

input._note: Images come from the 256 px resize cache (runs/cache/resized_256, shared with the CNN baselines). Test: CLIP's resize 224 + centre crop + CLIP mean/std. The app must standardise uploads the same way (dpd/resize_cache.standardise).

augmentation._note: Same as the CNN baselines except a milder crop scale (0.5-1 instead of 0.25-1), because CLIP's pretrained features expect whole-object views. No hue jitter: colour is diagnostic.

validation._note: Same procedure as v4.2 but 1 split instead of 3: each split is now a full training run with the image encoder in the loop (images instead of cached embeddings). Note v4.2 showed one split can mis-set gamma, so treat v5's gamma with that caveat. v5.8: n_splits 1 -> 3 (seeds seed, seed+1, seed+2); selection uses the mean validation HM over splits, as in v4.2.

training._note: Prompt vectors as v4.2 (AdamW lr 2e-4, weight decay 0, logit scale 100, loss weights pair 1 / crop 0.5 / disease 0.5). max_epochs 30 -> 15 (v4.1/v4.2 selected epochs 13-18 with cached features; each epoch now re-encodes every image). Batch 256 -> 64 for GPU memory with gradients through 4 image-encoder blocks.

posthoc._note: NEW (v5.11): primitive fusion, so the branch features are used at prediction time: pair score + a * crop-branch score + b * disease-branch score (dpd/fusion.py), a and b chosen on validation with the epoch and gamma. Grids as v9 (which reached the 4.0 edge only in a smoke test). LoRA scale fixed at 1 (not part of this method). The run also logs plain scoring and a paired bootstrap of fused vs plain on validation.

runtime._note: Gradient checkpointing on the text encoder as before. 4 dataloader workers read the resize cache.
